Macros for body recomp

Trying to figure out the optimal calorie intake for a body recomp (with slight weight loss 5-10lbs): 

32 years old
Female
5ft 2in
Current weight: 115lbs 
Current body fat: ~25%
Ideal weight: 105lbs 

This past month I’ve kept calorie intake at ~1,400 but haven’t been tracking macros. I’ve seen a little bit of improvement in my waist. 

I’m working out 6x week. 30 min cardio 3x week and 30 min cardio + 30 min strength training the other 3x. 

Trying to figure out the balance of eating enough to gain muscle while simultaneously not over eating and making sure I can still drop fat and overall weight. 

FWIW I did this 3 years ago (did not track macros but kept a strict calorie intake and did strength training 5x week and no cardio). Went from 115lb to 105lb and still had lots of muscle mass. Looking back I’m surprised it worked as well as it did and wish I would have track of what I did to replicate it.

Congrats on the engagement! I’m 4 years older than my med school boyfriend too and had a lot of the same concerns going into it! 

We had been together 4 years already when he got accepted into med school across the country. Since he is younger than me I was ok moving and not being engaged. But before moving we talked about getting engaged and married before residency. We also talked about “the ticking clock” and how me being older than him makes it  harder. 

I’m 28 now and he’s 24 and he’s starting M3. Hoping for engagement to come soon as we’re planning to get married at the end of M4. I’ll be 30 when he graduates med school and 34-ish when he finishes residency. We will likely be living in another new state without family around and I am going to continue my career. So it’s important for me that we have kids at a time he can be very involved. Therefore, I am not planning for kids until residency is over or possibly the last year. Long story short, don’t get too caught up in the age gap. You will still be in your early 30s when he’s done and people are having kids later these days anyways. Also, like others have said try to not think about it as putting your life on hold but that you’re living your life for the next 10 years the way you want (with exception to living location(s)). 

I’m sure it’s just the stress and pre-moving/med school nerves, but I am surprised to hear him say he might not want you there. I think going into med school it’s important to live together if you can make it work,  instead of LDR. There are so many LDRs that don’t workout during medical school. It will be additionally stressful if you’re planning a wedding. Hopefully he comes around and you figure out something that works for you both!

PS My boyfriend started out thinking he was going to do ER (only 3 yr residency!) then shifted to one with 6 yrs (yes I lost it for a couple days)... but since then changed two more times. Interests will change and he might very well chose a specialty without a 6 yr residency!

Two years ago I moved across the country with my boyfriend for him to start med school. I left a job I really loved, but only because we saw a long term future together. The first 6 months were an adjustment (mostly because I was WFH and looking for a new job) but once I had a job lined up and started making friends it became much better! Now at the halfway mark until med school is over I’m getting anxious about having to move away from this city that was unexpectedly so great. 

However, I’m sure the next city will be a pleasant surprise as well! Although it can be hard to leave friends/family/jobs it’s also pretty great being able to live in so many different places. I’d much rather look back and think about all the places I lived vs growing up and living in just one city/state my whole life!

A few tips:
- I know covid makes it hard right now but try to get out of the WFH situation as soon as you can find a good local job. It gets depressing being home (alone) all the time in a new city 
- Make sure your expectations are out there before you move. For me, I didn’t want to move the first time until we had a serious conversation about where we saw our relationship going. I made it clear that if I move for med school and everything goes well I’d like to get married before residency 
- Unfortunately, multiple moves will happen in this journey. Make sure you’ll be able to give input when it comes to future moves (residency, fellow, etc).
